recognize_zh: 低倍下視野中六顆嗜中性球周圍都黏附一圈小紫色血小板，排列成花環狀（rosette），而背景中游離血小板很少，這就是血小板衛星現象（platelet satellitism），會造成假性血小板減少。
features: Multiple neutrophils each rimmed by numerous adherent platelets forming rosettes
Platelets are small, purple, granular fragments of normal size attached around the cell membrane
Paucity of free platelets in the background
Neutrophils otherwise show segmented nuclei without toxic change evident at this magnification
Thick area of smear with overlapping red cells, limiting red cell morphology assessment
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low-medium power shows multiple neutrophils, each surrounded by a rosette of adherent platelets, while relatively few platelets lie free in the background. The platelets appear morphologically normal in size and granularity. The field is from a thick area with overlapping red cells, limiting assessment of red cell morphology. Findings are consistent with platelet satellitism, an in vitro EDTA-dependent phenomenon that can cause spurious thrombocytopenia on automated counts; repeat count in a citrate or heparin tube and smear review is recommended.

ddx.vs: Platelet clumps form free-lying aggregates of platelets in the background or at the feathered edge rather than rosettes encircling neutrophils; both cause pseudothrombocytopenia.
Phagocytosed platelets lie within the neutrophil cytoplasm in vacuoles, whereas satellite platelets adhere to the external cell surface.
In true thrombocytopenia platelets are sparse throughout the smear without rosettes or clumps, and counts remain low in citrate-anticoagulated samples.
